summary: Follow-up plan of RD.7, crystalline comparison and Weil-factor export, building on the 11 RD.7 nodes of the reviewed parent packet. It plans the proof of the rational rigid–crystalline comparison for smooth proper varieties through Berthelot's morphism from the tube to the completed PD envelope and its quasi-isomorphism property (Berthelot, Finitude et pureté, Proposition 1.9), and Ogus's comparison with coefficients and Frobenius after Shiho's Theorem 2.36. It plans the characteristic-zero weight-separation theorem and Fatou's lemma on which the integrality and the ℓ-independence of the Weil factors rest, and the degree-one statement that the crystalline Frobenius polynomial of an abelian variety is its Weil polynomial. For point counting it plans the corrected reduction bounds in Kedlaya's algorithm, the integral crystalline lattice that controls the denominators of the Frobenius matrix, and Tuitman's certified algorithm for curves with a map to P^1 with its precision bounds. It states the Fresán–Sabbah–Yu Kloosterman applications, whose p-adic comparison inputs lie above this roadmap's tier. No implementation is claimed.

nodes.title: Berthelot's comparison morphism from the tube to the completed PD envelope
nodes.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], X a separated k-scheme of finite type and i : X → P a closed immersion into a p-adic formal W-scheme P that is smooth over W in a neighbourhood of X. Let sp : ]X[_P → X be the specialisation map from the tube (RD.3/tube), 𝔦 ⊂ O_P the ideal of X (it contains p), D = D_P(X) the divided power envelope of 𝔦 compatible with the canonical divided powers of pW, and D̂ its p-adic completion, a sheaf of O_P-algebras supported on X. There is a unique morphism of sheaves of O_P-algebras c_{X,P} : sp_* O_{]X[_P} → D̂ ⊗_Z Q that is continuous on affine opens; it commutes with the derivations of O_P, so it induces a morphism of complexes of sheaves on X, c_{X,P} : sp_*Ω^•_{]X[_P} → D̂ ⊗_{O_P} Ω^•_{P/W} ⊗ Q (Berthelot's (1.9.2)). On an affine open U = Spf A of P on which 𝔦 is generated by f_1, …, f_r, the map factors through the closed tube of radius λ = |p|^{1/p}, whose ring of functions is A{T_1, …, T_r}/(f_j^p − pT_j) ⊗ Q, and sends T_j to (p − 1)!·f_j^{[p]}. No properness or smoothness of X is needed for the construction. With coefficients: for a crystal M of finite locally free O_{X/W}-modules with value M_D on D̂ and associated convergent isocrystal E on ]X[_P (RD.3), the same recipe gives c_{X,P}(M) : sp_*(E ⊗ Ω^•_{]X[_P}) → M_D ⊗ Ω^•_{P/W} ⊗ Q.
hypotheses: k perfect of characteristic p; X separated of finite type over k.
i : X → P closed immersion into a p-adic formal W-scheme P, smooth over W in a neighbourhood of X.
Divided powers on 𝔦 are taken compatible with the canonical divided powers of (p) ⊂ W.
proofSteps: Affine description: on U = Spf A with 𝔦 = (p, f_1, …, f_r) the tube is the rigid subspace |f_j| < 1, and its functions restrict to the closed sub-tube |f_j| ≤ |p|^{1/p}, whose affinoid algebra is A{T}/(f_j^p − pT_j) ⊗ Q (Berthelot, Finitude, proof of Proposition 1.9).

Since f_j^p = p!·f_j^{[p]} in D, the assignment T_j ↦ (p − 1)!·f_j^{[p]} kills f_j^p − pT_j and defines an A-algebra map A[T]/(f_j^p − pT_j) → D; it extends to the p-adic completions and, after inverting p, to the stated map; uniqueness: it is the only continuous A ⊗ Q-algebra map between these rings (CrystallineCohomology:CR.0/pd-envelope, CR.0/completed-envelope).

The local maps agree on overlaps by uniqueness, so they glue to c_{X,P}; continuity gives compatibility with derivations, hence a map of de Rham complexes, and functoriality in (X, P) follows from uniqueness.

Coefficients: the crystal M evaluated on D̂ is a module with integrable connection (CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/taylor-equivalence), and its analytification on the tube is the convergent isocrystal E (RD.3/restriction-to-convergent); the module version of the same map is compatible with the connections (Shiho, Relative log convergent cohomology I, §2, p. 31, constructs the log and relative version 'by the same method').
acceptance: For X = Spec k inside P = Spf W⟨t⟩ (𝔦 = (p, t)), the map sends a function Σ b_n t^n on the open unit disc to Σ b_n n!·t^{[n]}.
For a smooth affine X with a smooth formal lift P (𝔦 = pO_P), D̂ = O_P, ]X[_P = P_K and c_{X,P} is the identity of O_P ⊗ Q.

nodes.title: Berthelot's comparison morphism is a quasi-isomorphism for smooth X
nodes.statement: In the situation of RD.7/tube-to-envelope-comparison-map, assume X smooth over k. Then c_{X,P} : sp_*Ω^•_{]X[_P} → D̂ ⊗_{O_P} Ω^•_{P/W} ⊗ Q is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of sheaves of K_0-vector spaces on X, and so is its version c_{X,P}(M) with coefficients in a crystal M of finite locally free O_{X/W}-modules. The induced isomorphism in the derived category does not depend on the embedding P, and is compatible with the canonical isomorphisms between two embeddings on each side. If X is in addition proper, taking hypercohomology on X gives the canonical isomorphism H^i_rig(X/K_0) ≅ H^i_crys(X/W) ⊗_W K_0 of RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison, now with its proof.
hypotheses: X smooth separated of finite type over the perfect field k.
i : X → P closed immersion into a p-adic formal W-scheme smooth near X.
proofSteps: The assertion is local on X and on P, so P = Spf A may be taken affine and X = Spec A/𝔦 affine and smooth.

Independence of the embedding on both sides, compatibly with c: for two embeddings X → P and X → P' compare both with the diagonal embedding in P × P'. On the tube side the projection ]X[_{P×P'} → ]X[_P is locally a fibration in open polydiscs (RD.3/weak-fibration-theorem) and the de Rham complex of an open polydisc is a resolution, which is the content of RD.4/independence-of-embedding; on the PD side, CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/smooth-ambient-comparison and CR.2/embedding-independence give the canonical quasi-isomorphisms at each finite level W_n, and the p-adic version is their derived limit, which equals D̂ ⊗ Ω^• because on affines the transition maps are surjective (CR.0/completed-envelope). Naturality of c in the embedding (API tubeToEnvelope_naturality) makes the squares commute.

Choose a smooth formal lift P' of the smooth affine X: lifts exist at every finite level because the obstructions lie in H^2(X, T_X) ⊗ I = 0 on an affine (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/deformations-of-smooth-schemes), and the compatible system defines a smooth affine formal scheme (Elkik's theorem is the usual citation; Kedlaya, Notes on isocrystals, Definition 2.1).

For the lift, 𝔦' = pO_{P'}, the PD envelope is O_{P'} itself (p has divided powers in W), the tube is P'_K, and c is the identity (API tubeToEnvelope_lift). By the previous two steps c_{X,P} is a quasi-isomorphism (Berthelot, Finitude, end of the proof of Proposition 1.9).

Coefficients: the same three steps apply with M_D ⊗ Ω^• on the PD side (CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/smooth-ambient-comparison for a quasi-coherent crystal) and E ⊗ Ω^• on the tube side (RD.4/independence-of-embedding for the coefficient E); this is Shiho's proof of Theorem 2.36 with trivial log structures and base Spf W.

For X proper: RΓ_rig(X/K_0) = RΓ(X, sp_*Ω^•_{]X[_P}) because the strict neighbourhoods are the whole tube and R^q sp_* vanishes for q > 0 on the quasi-Stein inverse images of affines (RD.4/proper-rigid-equals-convergent; Berthelot, Finitude, proof of 1.9), and RΓ_crys(X/W) ⊗ Q = RΓ(X, D̂ ⊗ Ω^•) ⊗ Q because X is quasi-compact; take hypercohomology of the quasi-isomorphism. A non-embeddable proper X is handled by a finite Zariski cover by embeddable opens and Čech descent on both sides (CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/crystalline-descent; RD.4/rigid-cohomology).
acceptance: X = A^1_k with the lift P = Spf W⟨t⟩: c is the identity and both sides compute the de Rham cohomology of the Tate algebra K_0⟨t⟩, whose H^1 is infinite-dimensional (the form Σ_k p^k t^{p^{2k}−1}dt has formal primitive with coefficients p^{−k}, so it is not exact); this is why the rigid form of the comparison needs X proper.
X = P^1_k: H^0 = K_0, H^1 = 0, H^2 = K_0 on both sides, and the comparison sends the rigid class of a rational point to its crystalline class.

The map is a quasi-isomorphism without being an isomorphism of complexes: for X = Spec k ⊂ Spf W⟨t⟩ the degree-zero terms differ (API test tubeToEnvelope_not_surjective), yet both complexes resolve K_0.

nodes.title: Ogus's comparison: crystalline cohomology of an F-crystal versus rigid cohomology of its isocrystal
nodes.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], X a smooth proper k-scheme and M a crystal of finite locally free O_{X/W}-modules on the crystalline site of X over W (CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/crystal). Let E be the associated convergent isocrystal; because X is proper it is an overconvergent isocrystal (RD.3/restriction-to-convergent). Then there are canonical isomorphisms H^i_crys(X/W, M) ⊗_W K_0 ≅ H^i_rig(X/K_0, E) for every i, functorial in M and in X, compatible with finite extensions K/K_0 (RD.4/finite-flat-base-change). If (M, Φ) is an F-crystal relative to the Witt vector Frobenius σ (CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/frobenius-map) and E carries the induced Frobenius structure, the isomorphisms carry the σ-semilinear crystalline Frobenius to the Frobenius of RD.4/frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology; for k = F_q, q = p^f, the K_0-linear map φ^f on the left corresponds to the linear q-Frobenius F of RD.6/linear-q-frobenius. For M = O_{X/W} this is RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison together with RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison. Properness is used only to identify the convergent cohomology of E with its rigid cohomology; the crystalline–convergent isomorphism itself holds for smooth X (Ogus; Shiho, Theorem 2.36), while for non-proper X crystalline cohomology is not finite and is not the right comparison object (Kedlaya, Notes on isocrystals, Remark 8.5).
hypotheses: k perfect; X smooth and proper over k.
M a crystal of finite locally free O_{X/W}-modules; E its convergent (hence overconvergent) isocrystal.
For the Frobenius statement: (M, Φ) an F-crystal relative to σ, with E given the induced Frobenius structure.
proofSteps: Choose a finite Zariski cover of X by opens admitting closed immersions into p-adic formal W-schemes smooth near them; rigid cohomology of E is computed on the tubes because X is proper (RD.4/proper-rigid-equals-convergent, RD.4/rigid-cohomology), and crystalline cohomology of M by the completed PD envelopes (CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/smooth-ambient-comparison).

The coefficient version of Berthelot's morphism (RD.7/tube-to-envelope-comparison-map, API tubeToEnvelope_coeff) is a quasi-isomorphism (RD.7/comparison-map-quasi-isomorphism); glue by Čech descent and take hypercohomology.
Functoriality in M is that of the evaluation of crystals; base change to K uses RD.4/finite-flat-base-change.

Frobenius: the absolute Frobenius of X over σ induces the crystalline Frobenius (CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/frobenius-map) and, through any Frobenius lift on the embeddings, the rigid Frobenius (RD.4/frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology, independent of the lift by RD.4/frobenius-independent-of-lift); naturality of the comparison morphism for morphisms of pairs lying over σ identifies them. Over F_q, σ^f = id on W(F_q), so φ^f is linear and equals F (RD.6/linear-q-frobenius).
acceptance: M = O_{X/W}: the theorem is the inherited rigid–crystalline comparison; for X = P^1 both sides are K_0, 0, K_0 with Frobenius 1, ·, p·σ.
Rank-one F-crystal on X = Spec F_p: M = W with Φ = p^a gives H^0_crys = Z_p with Frobenius p^a and H^0_rig = Q_p with Frobenius p^a.

Non-example: for X = A^1_k (not proper) H^1_crys(A^1/W) ⊗ Q is the de Rham H^1 of K_0⟨t⟩, which is infinite-dimensional (the form Σ_k p^k t^{p^{2k}−1}dt is not exact), whereas H^1_rig(A^1/K_0) = 0; properness cannot be dropped from the rigid form.

nodes.title: Rational power series descend to Q and have integral normalised numerator and denominator (Fatou)
nodes.statement: (a) Descent of rationality. Let k ⊂ L be fields and f ∈ k[[t]]. If there are A, B ∈ L[t] with B(0) ≠ 0 and Bf = A in L[[t]], then there are such A, B in k[t]; that is, k[[t]] ∩ L(t) = k(t) inside L((t)). (b) Local Fatou. Let ℓ be a prime (ℓ = p allowed), f ∈ 1 + tZ_ℓ[[t]], and G, H ∈ Q_ℓ[t] coprime with G(0) = H(0) = 1 and Hf = G. Then G, H ∈ Z_ℓ[t]. (c) Global Fatou. If f ∈ 1 + tZ[[t]] lies in Q(t), there are unique coprime A, B ∈ 1 + tZ[t] with f = A/B; the reciprocal roots of A and of B are algebraic integers. The equality is in Q[[t]], and A, B do not depend on any auxiliary field in which f was first shown to be rational.
hypotheses: (a): any field extension k ⊂ L.
(b): f has ℓ-adically integral coefficients and constant term 1; G, H coprime with constant term 1.
(c): f has integer coefficients and constant term 1.
proofSteps: (a) Bf = A with deg A ≤ N, deg B ≤ M is a system of linear equations over k in the coefficients of A and B (the vanishing of the Hankel determinants of order > M of the coefficient sequence of f beyond degree N); a system with coefficients in k that has a nonzero solution over L has one over k, and B(0) ≠ 0 may be arranged after cancelling a power of t (Deligne, Weil I, proof of (1.7) ⇒ (1.6), p. 276; Milne, Lemma 27.9).

(b) Work in a finite extension of Q_ℓ splitting H with the extended absolute value. If a reciprocal root α of H had |α| > 1, then α^{−1} lies in the open unit disc, where f converges because its coefficients are bounded by 1, and evaluating Hf = G at α^{−1} gives G(α^{−1}) = 0, contradicting coprimality. So the reciprocal roots of H have absolute value at most 1; since 1/f ∈ 1 + tZ_ℓ[[t]] and (1/f)G = H, the same holds for G. Elementary symmetric functions of elements of absolute value ≤ 1 have absolute value ≤ 1 (Milne, Lemma 27.10, with the non-strict inequality at the boundary).

(c) Write f = A/B in lowest terms over Q with A(0) = B(0) = 1 (possible since f(0) = 1 and B(0) ≠ 0 after (a)); apply (b) at every prime ℓ to get A, B ∈ Z_ℓ[t] for all ℓ, hence A, B ∈ Z[t]. Reciprocal roots of a polynomial in 1 + tZ[t] are roots of its reverse, a monic integer polynomial, hence algebraic integers (Deligne, Weil I, p. 276, 'lemme de Fatou').
acceptance: Integrality cannot be dropped: f = 1/(1 − t/2) ∈ 1 + tQ[[t]] is rational with denominator 1 − t/2 ∉ Z[t].
Coprimality cannot be dropped in (b): G = H = 1 − t/ℓ with f = 1 shows that a non-reduced presentation need not be integral.
Boundary case: f = 1/(1 − t) ∈ 1 + tZ_ℓ[[t]] has a reciprocal root of absolute value exactly 1, so the bound in (b) is ≤ 1, not < 1.

nodes.title: Weight separation: pure factors of a rational zeta function are unique, rational and integral
nodes.statement: Let q > 1 be an integer and R ∈ 1 + tZ[[t]] ∩ Q(t), written R = A/B with A, B ∈ 1 + tZ[t] coprime (RD.7/rational-zeta-descent-and-fatou). Let L be a field of characteristic 0 with algebraic closure L̄ and P_0, …, P_N ∈ 1 + tL[t] with ∏_{i=0}^{N} P_i^{(−1)^{i+1}} = R in L[[t]], such that every reciprocal root of P_i in L̄ is algebraic over Q and a Weil q-number of weight i (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/weil-q-number). Then: (1) the P_i are pairwise coprime, and A = ∏_{i odd} P_i, B = ∏_{i even} P_i in L[t]; (2) for each i there is a unique Π_i ∈ 1 + tZ[t] whose image in L[t] is P_i, namely Π_i = ∏(1 − αt)^{m(α)}, the product over the reciprocal roots α of A (i odd) or B (i even) that are Weil q-numbers of weight i, with their multiplicities m(α) as roots; (3) the reciprocal roots of Π_i are algebraic integers and deg Π_i = deg P_i; (4) if (P'_i) is a second family over another field L' of characteristic 0 with the same R and the same purity property, then P_i and P'_i are images of the same Π_i. The integrality in (2)–(3) comes from Fatou's lemma and the separation of weights, not from the alternating product alone; without purity, cancellation between degrees can occur and the factors are not determined by R.
hypotheses: q > 1 an integer; R ∈ 1 + tZ[[t]] rational.
L a field of characteristic 0; P_i ∈ 1 + tL[t] with alternating product R.
Every reciprocal root of P_i is a Weil q-number of weight i (all complex conjugates of absolute value q^{i/2}).
proofSteps: Weights separate: a Weil q-number has a unique weight (DWP.0/weil-q-number), so P_i and P_j have no common root for i ≠ j; hence ∏_{i odd} P_i and ∏_{i even} P_i are coprime and their quotient is a reduced presentation of R over L. Comparing with the reduced presentation A/B over Q (both normalised by constant term 1) gives (1).

Let K ⊂ L̄ be the splitting field over Q of AB. The set of reciprocal roots of AB of weight i, with multiplicities, is stable under Gal(K/Q), because being a Weil q-number of weight i depends only on the minimal polynomial over Q (DWP.0/weil-q-number). So the coefficients of Π_i are fixed by Gal(K/Q) and lie in Q (mathlib:IsGalois.mem_range_algebraMap_iff_fixed).

The reverse of Π_i is a monic factor in Q[T] of the monic integral reverse of A or B, so by Gauss's lemma it has integer coefficients (mathlib:IsIntegrallyClosed.eq_map_mul_C_of_dvd); equivalently its roots are algebraic integers by RD.7/rational-zeta-descent-and-fatou (c).
Uniqueness and (4): Π_i is described by R alone, so any second pure family gives the same polynomials (Deligne, Weil I, end of the proof of (1.7) ⇒ (1.6), p. 277).
acceptance: Elliptic curve E/F_7, y^2 = x^3 + x + 1: R = (1 − 3t + 7t^2)/((1 − t)(1 − 7t)) and Π_1 = 1 − 3t + 7t^2, whose roots have absolute value 7^{−1/2}.

Purity is needed: P_0 = 1, P_1 = P_2 = 1 − 2t give the alternating product R = 1, as do P_0 = P_1 = P_2 = 1, so R does not determine the factors; the hypothesis excludes this because 2 cannot be a Weil q-number of weight 1 and of weight 2.
Genus-two curve y^2 = x^5 + x + 3 over F_7: Π_1 = 1 + 3t + 7t^2 + 21t^3 + 49t^4 (PARI/GP hyperellcharpoly), with all roots of absolute value 7^{−1/2}.

sources.match: From purity of every eigenvalue the factors P_i are pairwise coprime, so the cohomological product is already reduced; each factor's roots are the roots of the reduced numerator or denominator with the right absolute value, a Galois-stable set, so the factor has rational, then (Gauss, or integrality of the reciprocal roots) integral coefficients independent of the cohomology theory.
Summary statement that the factors P_i are integral and independent of ℓ once purity holds.

sources.locator: §6.6, statement (c) and its proof, pp. 51–52
sources.match: Deduces from rigid Weil II (Theorem 6.6.2) and Poincaré duality that H^i_rig of a smooth proper variety is ι-pure of weight i for every ι, the purity input that this theorem turns into integral, realisation-independent factors.

nodes.title: The crystalline Frobenius polynomial of an abelian variety is its Weil polynomial
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety of dimension g over F_q, q = p^f, W = W(F_q), K_0 = W[1/p], π_A ∈ End(A) its q-Frobenius endomorphism (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.1/frobenius-endomorphism-over-a-finite-field) and P_A(T) = det(T − V_ℓπ_A | V_ℓA) ∈ Z[T] its characteristic polynomial, independent of ℓ ≠ p (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6/characteristic-polynomial-on-tate-module). Conventions: V_ℓA is the covariant rational Tate module, on which π_A acts as the arithmetic Frobenius x ↦ x^q of Gal(F̄_q/F_q) acts on torsion points; H^1_et(A_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ) = Hom(V_ℓA, Q_ℓ), on which the geometric Frobenius acts as the transpose of V_ℓπ_A; φ is the σ-semilinear crystalline Frobenius on the contravariant H^1_crys(A/W). Then: (1) the K_0-linear map φ^f on H^1_crys(A/W) ⊗ K_0 has characteristic polynomial P_A(T), so P_1(A, t) := det(1 − tφ^f | H^1_crys(A/W) ⊗ K_0) = t^{2g}P_A(1/t) = det(1 − t·Frob_q | H^1_et(A_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ)); (2) for every i, det(1 − tφ^f | H^i_crys ⊗ K_0) = ∏_{|I| = i}(1 − α_I t), where α_1, …, α_{2g} are the roots of P_A and α_I = ∏_{j ∈ I} α_j; (3) for an elliptic curve E given by a Weierstrass model over F_q, P_1(E, t) = 1 − a t + q t^2 with a = q + 1 − #E(F_q) the Frobenius trace (tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.frobeniusTrace). No inversion of the Frobenius and no dualisation changes the characteristic polynomial: transposition preserves it, and the geometric/arithmetic dictionary is absorbed by the contravariance of H^1.
hypotheses: A an abelian variety over F_q, q = p^f; ℓ ≠ p.
Crystalline Frobenius taken relative to the Witt vector Frobenius σ of W(F_q), so φ^f is K_0-linear.
proofSteps: Degree one from all degrees: A is projective, so RD.7/ell-adic-comparison-smooth-projective (Katz–Messing) gives det(1 − tφ^f | H^i_crys ⊗ K_0) = det(1 − t·Frob_q | H^i_et(A_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ)) for every i.

ℓ-adic side: H^1_et(A_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ) ≅ Hom(V_ℓA, Q_ℓ) Frobenius-equivariantly, with geometric Frobenius the transpose of V_ℓπ_A (request to ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6); a transpose has the same characteristic polynomial, so the ℓ-adic factor is the reverse of P_A.
Higher degrees: H^i_et = ∧^i H^1_et, so its Frobenius factor is ∏_{|I|=i}(1 − α_I t) (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.1/point-counts-of-abelian-varieties); combine with the first step.

Elliptic curves: P_A(T) = T^2 − aT + q with a = Tr π_A = q + 1 − deg(1 − π_A) = q + 1 − #E(F_q) (DWP.1/point-counts-of-abelian-varieties), which is Tau Ceti's WeierstrassCurve.frobeniusTrace for an elliptic model.
acceptance: y^2 = x^3 + x + 1 over F_7: #E(F_7) = 5, a = 3, P_1 = 1 − 3t + 7t^2; the crystalline polynomial T^2 − 3T + 7 has a unit root in Z_7 (E ordinary).

y^2 = x^3 + x over F_5: #E(F_5) = 4, a = 2, slopes 0 and 1; y^2 = x^3 − x over F_3: a = 0, φ has characteristic polynomial T^2 + 3 with slopes 1/2, 1/2 (agreeing with CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/elliptic-frobenius).
Supersingular y^2 = x^3 + x over F_7 and its base change to F_49: P_1 = 1 + 7t^2 and (1 + 7t)^2.
Degenerate g = 0 (A = Spec F_q): H^0 only, P_0 = 1 − t.

sources.locator: proof of Theorem 5.1.6, p. 25 (arXiv v4)
sources.match: Uses that the overconvergent F-isocrystal R^1f_crys,*O of an abelian scheme is pure, by the Riemann hypothesis for abelian varieties (the crystalline Frobenius eigenvalues on H^1 of each fibre are Weil numbers of weight 1), and that the linear Frobenius on the crystalline cohomology of a fibre is semisimple because it is central in its endomorphism algebra.
Records that Katz and Messing proved a crystalline version of the Weil conjectures resting on Deligne's theorem, which in degree one is the statement for abelian varieties.

nodes.title: Denominator bounds in the reduction of hyperelliptic differentials (Kedlaya Lemma 2, corrected Lemma 3)
nodes.statement: Let p be odd, q = p^n, Z_q = W(F_q), Q ∈ Z_q[x] monic of degree d = 2g + 1 with squarefree reduction, and A† the dagger algebra of the affine curve y^2 = Q(x) with the Weierstrass points removed (y invertible). The minus part H^1(A†)^− of its Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology has basis x^i dx/y, 0 ≤ i ≤ 2g − 1 (Edixhoven, Proposition 4.3.2). (a) (Kedlaya, Lemma 2; Edixhoven, Lemma 4.3.4.) For m ≥ 0 and B ∈ Z_q[x] of degree ≤ 2g, write B dx/y^{2m+1} = b dx/y + dφ with deg b ≤ 2g and φ = Σ_{j=1}^{m} F_j(x)/y^{2j−1}, deg F_j ≤ 2g; then p^{⌊log_p(2m+1)⌋}·b and p^{⌊log_p(2m+1)⌋}·F_j have coefficients in Z_q. (b) (Corrected Lemma 3; Edixhoven, Lemma 4.3.5; Harvey §3.) For m ≥ 0 and B ∈ Z_q[x] of degree ≤ 2g, write B·y^{2m+1} dx = b dx/y + dφ with deg b ≤ 2g and φ = Σ_{j=1}^{m+1} F_j(x)y^{2j−1}; then multiplication by p^{⌊log_p((2g+1)(2m+3) − 2)⌋} makes b and the F_j integral. Equivalently, for F(x)y^e dx with e > 0 odd the factor is p^{⌊log_p((2g+1)(e+2) − 2)⌋}. (c) Removing the remaining x^{2g} dx/y with the exact form dy = (Q'/2) dx/y divides by d = 2g + 1 and costs a further factor p^{v_p(2g+1)}. The bound printed as Lemma 3 in the source, p^{⌊log_p(2m+1)⌋}, is false, and so is the errata's replacement read literally in that lemma's indexing (sourceIssues E701).
hypotheses: p odd; Q monic of degree 2g + 1 over Z_q with squarefree reduction modulo p.
B ∈ Z_q[x] of degree at most 2g; m ≥ 0.
proofSteps: Negative powers: the poles of φ lie at the Weierstrass points T_i = (r_i, 0), where y is a uniformiser; expand dφ in y with integral coefficients for negative exponents, integrate termwise, and note that the denominators are the odd exponents of y down to −(2m+1); since the r_i are distinct modulo p, integrality of F_m(r_i) for all i forces integrality of F_m, and descending induction gives the rest (Kedlaya, proof of Lemma 2; Edixhoven, proof of 4.3.4).

Positive powers: the only pole is ∞, where v_∞(x) = −2, v_∞(y) = −d and z = x^{(d−1)/2}/y is a uniformiser with ι(z) = −z; expand dφ in z, whose coefficients are integral in exponents ≤ −d, integrate, and bound the denominators j + 1 by |j + 1| ≤ dm' + d − 2 for the even exponent m' = 2m + 2; the valuations v_∞(x^i y^j), 0 ≤ i < d, are distinct, which separates the F_j (Edixhoven, proof of 4.3.5).
The last reduction uses dy and divides by the leading coefficient d of Q' (Edixhoven, p. 17).
These bounds are what the working precision of RD.7/kedlaya-point-counting-certification absorbs (Harvey §3 uses (b) with e = −p(2k + 1) + 2j).
acceptance: Q = x^3 + x + 1, p = 5 (good reduction: disc = −31), m = 0: y dx = Q dx/y reduces to (2/5 x + 3/5) dx/y + d((2/5)xy), so the factor 5 = 5^{⌊log_5 7⌋} of (b) is needed, while the printed Lemma 3 (factor 5^{⌊log_5 1⌋} = 1) and the errata formula with m = 0 (factor 5^{⌊log_5 1⌋} = 1) both fail (exact computation with rational arithmetic).
m = 0 in (a): B dx/y with deg B ≤ 2g − 1 is already reduced and needs no factor (p^{⌊log_p 1⌋} = 1).
For p > (2g + 1)(2m + 3) − 2 every factor in (a)–(b) is 1, matching the observation that large p needs no extra precision.

sources.locator: Lemma 2 and its proof, Lemma 3 as printed, p. 5 (arXiv v2)
sources.match: Lemma 2 bounds the denominators in reducing A(x)dx/y^{2m+1} by p^{⌊log_p(2m+1)⌋} through expansions at the Weierstrass points; Lemma 3 asserts the same bound for A(x)y^{2m+1}dx without proof.

sources.locator: list of errata, p. 1–2 (13 October 2003)
sources.match: Replaces 2m + 1 by d(m + 1) − 2 at the journal's page 331, line 8, and records Edixhoven's remark that the Frobenius matrix on the monomial basis is not integral.

Proves the basis statement, the negative-power bound p^{⌊log_p(m−1)⌋} for ay^{−m}dx/y (m even) and the positive-power bound p^{⌊log_p(dm+d−2)⌋} for ay^m dx/y (m even) by local expansions at the Weierstrass points and at infinity, and notes the extra division by d in the last step.

nodes.title: The crystalline lattice in hyperelliptic H^1 and the denominators of the Frobenius matrix
nodes.statement: In the situation of RD.7/kedlaya-reduction-denominators let C_Q be the smooth projective model of y^2 = Q(x) over Z_q, M = ⊕_{0 ≤ i ≤ 2g−1} Z_q·x^i dx/y ⊂ H^1(A†)^−, t a uniformiser at ∞ with ι(t) = −t (for example t = x^g/y), and L ⊆ M the submodule of those ω whose principal part at ∞, an element of (t^{−2g}Z_q[[t]]dt)/(t^{−1}Z_q[[t]]dt), is the differential of an element of t^{−2g+1}Z_q[[t]]/Z_q[[t]]. Then: (1) L is the image of H^1_dR(C_Q/Z_q) ≅ H^1_crys(C/Z_q) in H^1(A†)^− = H^1_rig(C/K), so the p-power Frobenius F_p (and every power of it) maps L into L; (2) M/L ≅ ⊕_{i odd, −(2g−1) ≤ i < 0} Z_q/iZ_q, so p^c M ⊆ L ⊆ M with c = ⌊log_p(2g − 1)⌋; (3) consequently the matrix of every power F_p^r on the basis x^i dx/y lies in p^{−c}M_{2g}(Z_q), and if the matrix of F_p is known modulo p^N then the n-fold σ-twisted product computing the q-power Frobenius is known modulo p^{N−(n−1)c}, whereas on a Z_q-basis of L all matrices are integral and the product loses no precision; (4) the matrix of F_p on the monomial basis is in general not integral (computations of Vercauteren; the reduction estimates allow denominators of valuation up to v_p(d) + ⌊log_p(d − 2/p)⌋).
hypotheses: p odd; Q ∈ Z_q[x] monic of degree 2g + 1 with squarefree reduction; g ≥ 1.
F_p a Frobenius lift on A† with x ↦ x^p (Kedlaya's lift), acting on H^1(A†)^−.
proofSteps: H^1_dR(C_Q/Z_q) is computed by the complex O(0·∞) → Ω^1(∞); twisting by m·∞ gives complexes C(m) whose quotient C(2g − 1)/C(0) is the principal-part differential in the statement, and the resulting diagram identifies L with the image of H^1(C(0)) = H^1_dR(C_Q/Z_q) and computes M/L (Edixhoven, Proposition 5.3.1 and its sketch; Tuitman, Counting points II, Proposition 4.5, gives the complete argument for general curves, generalising it).

H^1_dR(C_Q/Z_q) = H^1_crys(C/Z_q) with its Frobenius (CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/formal-and-end0 for the proper smooth lift, CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/smooth-curve-lift), and the Frobenius on H^1_rig(C/K) restricted from H^1(A†)^− is the crystalline one by RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison and RD.6/gysin-sequence-for-curves; so F_p(L) ⊆ L.
Since F_p is σ-semilinear, F_p(M) ⊆ F_p(p^{−c}L) = p^{−c}F_p(L) ⊆ p^{−c}M; the same for F_p^r.

Precision: let P_j be the exact product of the first j factors, which is the matrix of a power of Frobenius on M and so lies in p^{−c}M_{2g}(Z_q); an input error in p^N M_{2g}(Z_q) propagates to an error in p^{N−(j−1)c} after j factors by induction on j.
acceptance: g = 1, p ≥ 3: c = ⌊log_p 1⌋ = 0, so L = M and the matrix on dx/y, x dx/y is integral.
g = 2, p = 3: c = ⌊log_3 3⌋ = 1 and M/L ≅ Z_q/3Z_q (from i = −3), so one extra digit suffices.
Kedlaya's errata: the denominators on the monomial basis are bounded independently of the extension degree n, which is (3) with c = ⌊log_p(2g − 1)⌋.

sources.locator: §5.2, pp. 17–18, and Proposition 5.3.1 with its proof sketch, pp. 18–19
sources.match: Notes that the reduction estimates do not show integrality of the Frobenius matrix on x^i dx/y and that it often fails, and proves that the submodule of forms with integrable principal part at infinity is the image of integral de Rham (= crystalline) cohomology, stable under Frobenius, with quotient killed by p^{⌊log_p(2g−1)⌋}.

Explains that the Frobenius matrix on the monomial basis is not integral, that the denominators stay bounded, and that the submodule of forms whose expansion at infinity integrates over Z_q is Frobenius-stable and gives integral matrices.

nodes.title: Tuitman's Frobenius lift and cohomological reduction for curves with a map to P^1
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth projective curve of genus g over F_q, q = p^n, with a finite separable map x : X → P^1 of degree d_x and a rational function y generating the function field, satisfying an irreducible equation Q(x, y) = 0 monic in y of degree d_x; let Q ∈ Z_q[x, y] be a lift with the same support, still monic in y, Δ its discriminant in y, r = Δ/gcd(Δ, dΔ/dx), U = Spec Z_q[x, 1/r, y]/(Q) and R† its weak completion. Assume Tuitman's Assumption 1 in its corrected form: (1) matrices W^0 ∈ GL_{d_x}(Z_q[x, 1/r]) and W^∞ ∈ GL_{d_x}(Z_q[x, 1/x, 1/r]) give integral bases of the function field over Q_q[x] and over Q_q[1/x] whose reductions are integral bases over F_q[x] and F_q[1/x]; (2) the discriminant of r is a unit; (3) the discriminants of the reduced parts (quotients by the nilradicals) of the finite Z_q-algebras R^0/(r) and R^∞/(1/x) are units (June 2020 erratum). Then: (a) U is the complement of a smooth relative divisor D_X in a smooth proper curve X over Z_q with special fibre X (Tuitman, Proposition 2.3); (b) there is a σ-semilinear Frobenius lift F_p on R† with F_p(x) = x^p, computed by Newton iteration modulo p^{2^i} (Theorem 2.6); (c) cohomological reduction at the finite and infinite points produces a basis ω_1, …, ω_κ of H^1_rig(U) from algebraic differentials, whose first 2g elements span H^1_rig(X) (the kernel of the residue map), together with, for every overconvergent 1-form ν on U, its coordinates and an overconvergent primitive: ν = Σ_j c_jω_j + dh; (d) applied to F_p^*ω_i this gives the Frobenius matrix F and overconvergent functions f_i with F_p^*ω_i = Σ_j F_{ij}ω_j + df_i, the q-power Frobenius F^{(n)} = F^{σ^{n−1}}⋯F^{σ}F, and the reverse characteristic polynomial χ(T) = det(1 − F^{(n)}T | H^1_rig(X)), which equals the Weil factor P_1(X, T) of RD.7/weil-factor (so #X(F_{q^r}) = q^r + 1 − Tr(F^{(n)r}|H^1_rig(X))). Consumers apply (c) to further forms, for example to the right-hand sides of the equations for the Frobenius structure of a unipotent connection (Balakrishnan–Dogra–Müller–Tuitman–Vonk, (22)).
hypotheses: X smooth projective geometrically connected curve over F_q with a finite separable x : X → P^1 and a plane model Q monic in y.
Tuitman's Assumption 1 with condition (3) as corrected in June 2020.
proofSteps: (a): glue Spec R^0 and Spec R^∞ along U; flatness and regularity of both fibres (from the integral bases) give smoothness, and the unit discriminants give étaleness of the boundary (Tuitman, proof of Proposition 2.3).

(b): define F_p(1/r) and F_p(y) as limits of the Newton iterations α_{i+1} = α_i(2 − α_i r^σ(x^p)) and the analogous iteration for y with 1/Δ = g(x)/r(x)^m; convergence in R† is the Hensel argument for the étale map U → V (Tuitman, Theorem 2.6). This is an instance of RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra with a chosen form.

(c): reduce poles along r = 0 using the integral basis b^0 and the relation from d of b^0_j/r^ℓ, then poles above ∞ using b^∞; H^1_rig(X) is the kernel of the residue map on H^1_rig(U) (Tuitman, Theorem 3.11, quoted there as well known; here RD.6/gysin-sequence-for-curves), and the basis is chosen with ω_1, …, ω_{2g} spanning that kernel (Tuitman, §4.1, Step I).

(d): F is the matrix of the rigid Frobenius on H^1_rig(U) for the basis ω (RD.4/mw-comparison-for-affine-curves: the Frobenius on Ω^1_{R†}/dR† is independent of the lift); its characteristic polynomial on H^1_rig(X) is the Weil factor by RD.7/weil-factor and RD.6/monsky-washnitzer-fixed-point-formula.
acceptance: Hyperelliptic case: Q = y^2 − f(x), d_x = 2, with f squarefree of odd degree 2g + 1 and unit discriminant; Assumption 1 holds with W^0 = 1, and the algorithm recovers Kedlaya's: for y^2 = x^5 + x + 3 over F_7, χ(T) = 1 + 3T + 7T^2 + 21T^3 + 49T^4 and #X(F_7) = 11.
Genus zero: for x : P^1 → P^1 the identity (Q = y − x), H^1_rig(X) = 0 and χ = 1.

The printed Assumption 1(3) excludes every hyperelliptic curve: R^0/(r) = (Z_q[x]/(f))[y]/(y^2) is not reduced, so its discriminant is 0, while its reduced part Z_q[x]/(f) has unit discriminant; the corrected condition holds.

nodes.title: Certified precision for Tuitman's algorithm
nodes.statement: In the situation of RD.7/tuitman-frobenius-structure-algorithm, write χ(T) = det(1 − F^{(n)}T | H^1_rig(X)) ∈ Z[T]. Let e_0, e_∞ be the maximal ramification indices of x over the zeros of r and over ∞, ord_0(W), ord_∞(W^{−1}) the orders of the change-of-basis matrix W = (W^0)^{−1}W^∞, and put B = max_{1≤i≤g}(⌊log_p binom(4g, i) + ni/2⌋ + 1), δ_1 = ⌊log_p(−(ord_0(W) + 1)e_∞)⌋, δ_2 = ⌊log_p((⌊(2g−2)/d_x⌋ + 1)e_∞)⌋, δ = δ_1 + δ_2, f_1(m) = ⌊log_p(p(m − 1)e_0)⌋ + ⌊log_p(−(ord_∞(W^{−1}) + 1)e_∞)⌋ and f_2 = ⌊log_p(−p(ord_0(W) + 1)e_∞)⌋. Then: (1) χ is determined by its residue modulo p^B; (2) with Λ the Z_q-span of the reduction basis and Λ_cris the image of the log-crystalline H^1_cris(X, D_X), p^{δ_1}Λ ⊆ Λ_cris ⊆ p^{−δ_2}Λ, so ord_p(F) ≥ −δ; (3) knowing F modulo p^{B+δ} suffices to recover χ; (4) it suffices to run the computation at working p-adic precision N such that m − max(f_1(m), f_2) ≥ B + δ for every m ≥ N, and N can be taken in Õ(d_x d_y n). For the hyperelliptic case this recovers RD.7/hyperelliptic-integral-frobenius-lattice.
hypotheses: The hypotheses of RD.7/tuitman-frobenius-structure-algorithm (corrected Assumption 1).
proofSteps: (1): the coefficients of χ satisfy the functional equation and the Weil bounds of RD.7/weil-factor-export, so the first g of them are integers of absolute value at most binom(2g, i)q^{i/2} ≤ binom(4g, i)q^{i/2}/2 and are determined by their residues modulo p^B (Tuitman, Proposition 4.2; Kedlaya's reconstruction lemma).

(2): compare the log de Rham complex of (X, D_X) twisted by m·D_∞ with the untwisted one, whose H^1 is the log-crystalline H^1_cris(X, D_X) (CrystallineCohomology:CR.5/log-poincare, CR.5/p-adic-log-crystalline); the cokernel is killed by p^{⌊log_p(m e_∞)⌋}; Serre duality kills H^1(O(m_2D_∞)) for m_2 = ⌊(2g − 2)/d_x⌋ + 1 (Tuitman, Proposition 4.5). Since Frobenius preserves Λ_cris, ord_p(F) ≥ −δ (Corollary 4.6).
(3): compute χ in a basis of Λ_cris, where no precision is lost, and change basis (Proposition 4.7).
(4): track the denominators in reducing F_p(ω_i) at the finite and infinite points, bounded by f_1(m) and f_2 (Definition 4.8, Proposition 4.9).
acceptance: Hyperelliptic genus two over F_7 (y^2 = x^5 + x + 3): B = max(⌊log_7 8 + 1/2⌋ + 1, ⌊log_7 28 + 1⌋ + 1) = max(2, 3) = 3; |a_1| ≤ 4·7^{1/2} < 11 and |a_2| ≤ 6·7 = 42, and 7^3 = 343 > 2·42, so the residues modulo 343 determine a_1 = 3 and a_2 = 7.
Genus zero: the maximum over 1 ≤ i ≤ g is over the empty set; χ = 1 needs no precision.

The bound uses binom(4g, i) rather than the sharper 2·binom(2g, i); the certification is valid with either, and Kedlaya's N_1 of RD.7/kedlaya-point-counting-certification is the hyperelliptic instance.

nodes.title: Mieda's p-adic Picard–Lefschetz map for ordinary quadratic degenerations
nodes.statement: Let p be odd, L = Q_p(√−p) with ring of integers O_L and uniformiser √−p, and 𝒳 a proper flat Z_p-scheme of relative dimension N whose generic fibre is smooth and whose special fibre 𝒳_{F_p} is smooth outside finitely many ordinary quadratic points, each of which over O_L is formally given by an equation Q − u·(√−p)^2 with u a unit and Q a quadratic form defining a smooth quadric in P^N over O_L. Then: (1) the blow-up 𝒳'' of 𝒳 ⊗ O_L at these points is strictly semistable over O_L, with generic fibre 𝒳_L; (2) there is an injective L-linear map β : H^N_rig(𝒳_{F_p}/Q_p) ⊗ L → H^N_dR(𝒳_{Q_p}) ⊗ L, compatible with Frobenius when the right-hand side carries the Hyodo–Kato Frobenius of 𝒳'' (constructed with logarithmic de Rham–Witt complexes), and compatible with the restriction maps to the boundary strata (the commutative square of the Picard–Lefschetz formula); (3) if 𝒳_{F_p} is smooth, β is the rigid–de Rham comparison isomorphism of a smooth proper lift (RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison with CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/formal-and-end0).
hypotheses: p odd; 𝒳 proper flat over Z_p with smooth generic fibre.
Special fibre smooth away from finitely many ordinary quadratic points of the stated formal type over O_L = Z_p[√−p].
proofSteps: (1): blowing up an ordinary quadratic point of a family Q = u·π^2 gives two components meeting transversally, the exceptional quadric and the strict transform (Mieda, (2.3), as recalled by Fresán–Sabbah–Yu).

(2): the log-crystalline (Hyodo–Kato) cohomology of the special fibre of 𝒳'' carries Frobenius and monodromy (CrystallineCohomology:CR.6/log-de-rham-witt-model, CR.6/proper-log-rigid-hk) and is compared with de Rham cohomology of 𝒳_L by the Hyodo–Kato isomorphism (CrystallineCohomology:CR.6/hk-comparison); β is the composite of the map from rigid cohomology of the singular special fibre into it (Mieda, Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 2.13). Its injectivity and the Picard–Lefschetz square are Mieda's theorem; his paper was not read for this plan (recorded gap).
(3): when the special fibre is smooth there is nothing to blow up and the construction reduces to the comparison of rigid cohomology with de Rham cohomology of a lift.
acceptance: Fresán–Sabbah–Yu apply it to the compactification 𝒦̄' of the hypersurface 𝒦 attached to Sym^k Kl_2 (N = k − 1), where Q is the quadratic form Q_{ap} or Q_{bp} of their (5.6), (5.16).
Degenerate: no singular points, then 𝒳'' = 𝒳 ⊗ O_L is smooth and β is an isomorphism.

Non-example: without the extension to L = Q_p(√−p) the equation Q − u·p is not of the form Q − u·π^2 with π a uniformiser, and the blow-up over Z_p is not semistable; the ramified base change is necessary.

sources.locator: proof of Proposition 5.23, pp. 49–51 (arXiv v5)
sources.match: Recalls Mieda's p-adic Picard–Lefschetz formula: for ordinary quadratic singularities the blow-up over Z_p[√−p] is semistable, and there is a commutative diagram with an injective Frobenius-compatible map β from rigid cohomology of the special fibre to de Rham cohomology of the generic fibre, built with logarithmic de Rham–Witt complexes; in the smooth case β is the usual comparison isomorphism.

nodes.title: The p-adic realisation of the Kloosterman moments and middle rigid cohomology (Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, Proposition 5.23)
nodes.statement: Fix k > 1, a prime p, and a place of Q̄ above p; let V_{k,p} be the p-adic étale realisation of the Kloosterman motive M_k of Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, ϖ ∈ Q̄_p with ϖ^{p−1} = −p, K = Q_p(ϖ), and H^1_{rig,mid}(G_m/K, Sym^k Kl_2) = gr^W_{k+1}H^1_{rig,c}(G_m/K, Sym^k Kl_2) the middle rigid cohomology of the symmetric power of the Kloosterman F-isocrystal (RD.6), of dimension ⌊(k − 1)/2⌋ − δ_{4Z}(k) when p > k for odd k and p > k/2 for even k. Then: (1) V_{k,p} is de Rham as a representation of Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p); (2) if p is odd, V_{k,p} is semistable over Q_p(√−p) and there is an injection of Frobenius modules H^1_{rig,mid}(G_m/K, Sym^k Kl_2) → (V_{k,p} ⊗ B_st)^{Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p(√−p))} ⊗ K; (3) if moreover p > k for odd k (respectively p > k/2 for even k), V_{k,p} is crystalline and the map is an isomorphism with (V_{k,p} ⊗ B_cris)^{Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p)} ⊗ K.
hypotheses: k > 1; p prime (odd for (2)–(3)); the bounds on p in (3).
The period rings and functors of NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.5 and the p-adic comparison theorems C_dR and C_st (recorded gap).
proofSteps: (1): V_{k,p} is a subquotient of the cohomology of the smooth proper varieties 𝒦̄ or 𝒦̄', which is de Rham by the de Rham comparison theorem (gap), and subquotients of de Rham representations are de Rham.

(2), even k: the localisation spectral sequence for compact-support rigid cohomology of 𝒦̄' with its boundary (RD.4/excision-sequence) identifies the middle cohomology with gr^W_{k−1} of the kernel of the restriction α to the boundary; Mieda's injective β (RD.7/mieda-p-adic-picard-lefschetz) embeds that kernel into the kernel of the de Rham restriction over L, which by the semistable comparison theorem for the semistable model 𝒦̄'' (gap) is (V_{k,p}(1) ⊗ B_st)^{Gal(Q̄_p/L)} ⊗ L; β is Frobenius-compatible; extend scalars to K and take χ-isotypic parts.
(3): when 𝒦̄' is smooth, β is the comparison isomorphism and the kernel is pure of weight k − 1, giving the crystalline statement.
Odd k: the same argument with 𝒦' = 𝒦 (no first resolution).
acceptance: Dimensions from the formula ⌊(k − 1)/2⌋ − δ_{4Z}(k): k = 5, p > 5 gives 2; k = 8, p > 4 gives 3 − 1 = 2.
Small k: dimension 0 for k = 2 and k = 4 (so (3) is an equality of zero spaces) and 1 for k = 3 with p > 3.

sources.locator: §5.1.5, Proposition 5.23 and its proof, pp. 49–51 (arXiv v5)
sources.match: States and proves that the p-adic realisation is de Rham, semistable over Q_p(√−p) with an inclusion of the middle rigid cohomology into its D_st, and crystalline with equality under the bounds on p, using the localisation spectral sequence, Mieda's p-adic Picard–Lefschetz formula and the p-adic comparison theorem.

nodes.title: Newton above Hodge for Kloosterman moments and the valuation of their coefficients (Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, Corollary 5.27)
nodes.statement: Let k ≥ 1 and p an odd prime. The Newton polygon of the Frobenius module H^1_{rig,c}(G_m,F_p/K, Sym^k Kl_2) lies on or above the Hodge polygon of H^1_{dR,c}(G_m, Sym^k Kl_2), with the same endpoints when p > k for odd k and 2p > k for even k. Consequently, writing the moment L-function as Z_k(p; T) = Σ_n c_n T^n, one has v_p(c_n) ≥ n(n − 1) for every n and every p ≥ 3.
hypotheses: k ≥ 1; p odd.
RD.7/kloosterman-semistable-realization (with its recorded comparison-theorem gap).
proofSteps: The filtered (φ, N)-module (V_{k,p} ⊗ B_st)^{Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p(√−p))} of the semistable representation V_{k,p} is weakly admissible (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3, weak admissibility of D_st(V)): its Newton polygon lies above its Hodge polygon with the same endpoints.

Newton and Hodge polygons are additive for direct sums (Minkowski sums of the regions above them); the middle rigid cohomology injects into the Frobenius module of V_{k,p} (RD.7/kloosterman-semistable-realization (2)), so its Newton polygon lies above that of V_{k,p}, which lies above the Hodge polygon of the middle de Rham cohomology; under the bounds on p the two modules are equal and the endpoints agree.
Add back the trivial factor: one-dimensional with slopes 0 if k ≢ 0 mod 4, two-dimensional with slopes 0 and k/2 otherwise.

The valuation bound: c_n is, up to sign, the n-th elementary symmetric function of the Frobenius eigenvalues, so its valuation is at least the sum of the n smallest Newton slopes, hence at least the sum of the n smallest Hodge slopes; Fresán–Sabbah–Yu read off v_p(c_n) ≥ n(n − 1) from the Hodge numbers of the middle de Rham cohomology computed in their §5 (Remark 5.28). RD.6/slope-bounds-for-rigid-cohomology gives the coarser consistency check that all slopes lie in [0, k + 1].
acceptance: The bound v_p(c_n) ≥ n(n − 1) sharpens Haessig's (1 − 1/(p − 1))n(n − 1) for p ≥ 5 (Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, Remark 5.28).
Small n: the bound is empty for n = 0, 1 and for n = 2 asserts p^2 | c_2.

sources.locator: Corollary 5.27 and its proof, Remark 5.28 with (5.29), p. 51 (arXiv v5)
sources.match: Deduces from weak admissibility of D_st and the injection of Proposition 5.23 that the Newton polygon of compactly supported rigid cohomology lies above the Hodge polygon, with equal endpoints under the bounds on p, and that the coefficients of the moment L-function satisfy v_p(c_n) ≥ n(n − 1) for all p ≥ 3.

sourceIssues.printed: Condition (3) requires the discriminants of the finite Z_q-algebras R^0/(r(x)) and R^∞/(1/x) to be units.
sourceIssues.correction: Require unit discriminants only for their reduced parts (quotients by the nilradical).
sourceIssues.reason: The printed condition is sufficient but excludes every ramified map x, for example every hyperelliptic model y^2 = f(x): R^0/(r) = (Z_q[x]/(f))[y]/(y^2) is not reduced, so its discriminant is 0.
sourceIssues.known: Tuitman's erratum of June 2020 (jtuitman.github.io/erratum.pdf), crediting F. Vermeulen and W. Castryck
